---
title: Make a connector follow changes
description: Edit a ticket in Marfa and see the connector put it back, teach it to archive what the service drops, and read a failed run.
---

- **You'll build** on the connector from [Build a connector](/build/connector). It will archive a ticket the service no longer lists, and you'll watch it follow a changed list.
- **You need** that connector, built, with its key, and the ticket service still running. Keep the `plugins` checkout as your working folder.
- **You'll have** a connector that keeps its items matching the service, and a failed run you can read on your instance.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Edit a ticket in Marfa

The ticket service owns these records, and this connector carries nothing back to it, so the connector holds its items **read only**. Change a ticket's title anyway, using an ID and version from your own instance:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items update 01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9 --version 1 --prop title="Khruangbin, with support"
```

```text
updated tickets.ticket 01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9 "Khruangbin, with support" (version 2)
```

</Terminal>

Marfa takes the edit: `read_only` tells an app what the connector will do, and Marfa refuses nothing for it. Run the connector again, with the same settings as before:

<Terminal>

```bash
MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600 MARFA_API_KEY=<connector key> \
  TICKETS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4100 TICKETS_TOKEN=demo-token-1234 \
  node connectors/tickets/dist/main.js --once
```

```text
… warn title on 01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9 was changed in Marfa and put back from the vendor, which Marfa mirrors
… info run succeeded: created 0, updated 1, archived 0, unchanged 2, skipped 0
```

</Terminal>

The kit read the edit from your instance's event log and put back the service's title. A connector that carries changes back sends the edit to the vendor instead, as [Carry changes back](/build/connector-push) shows.

</Step>
<Step>

### Archive what the service dropped

So far the connector only adds and updates. Open `connectors/tickets/src/main.ts`, and ask `run` for two more helpers, `held` and `archive`:

```ts title="connectors/tickets/src/main.ts"
  async run({ env, signal, upsert, held, archive }) {
```

At the end of `run`, after the `upsert`, archive each item whose ticket the service no longer lists:

```ts title="connectors/tickets/src/main.ts"
    const listed = new Set(tickets.map((ticket) => `${account}:${ticket.id}`));
    const gone = (await held(ticketType.id))
      .map((row) => row.source_id)
      .filter((id): id is string => typeof id === "string" && !listed.has(id));
    await archive(ticketType.id, gone);
```

`held` returns the items the connector holds of a type. Reading a missing ticket as gone is safe only because **the service lists every ticket the account holds**. A vendor that answers part of its records, such as one page or open records only, says nothing about the rest.

An archived item leaves everyday lists but keeps its history, and comes back if the vendor lists it again. The bin is for people, so a connector never moves an item there. Build the connector again:

```bash
pnpm exec tsc -b connectors/tickets
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Change the list and run it again

In the service's `tickets.json`, change T-1041's venue, remove T-1187 and add a new ticket:

```json title="ticket-service/tickets.json"
[
  { "id": "T-1041", "event": "Khruangbin", "venue": "O2 Academy Brixton, London", "starts": "2026-12-04T19:30:00Z" },
  { "id": "T-1302", "event": "Arooj Aftab", "venue": "Union Chapel, London", "starts": "2027-02-20T19:00:00Z" }
]
```

The service reads the file on every request, so it needs no restart. Run the connector, and list every ticket, archived ones included:

<Terminal>

```bash
MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600 MARFA_API_KEY=<connector key> \
  TICKETS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4100 TICKETS_TOKEN=demo-token-1234 \
  node connectors/tickets/dist/main.js --once
```

```text
… info cleared: title on 01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9 was changed in Marfa and put back from the vendor, which Marfa mirrors (this run reached its check and did not find it again)
… info run succeeded: created 1, updated 1, archived 1, unchanged 0, skipped 0
```

```bash
marfa items list --type tickets.ticket --state any
```

```text
id                                    type            when                      title        state
01a1f170-4a6d-7398-a70b-a93313fa3e19  tickets.ticket  2027-02-20T19:00:00.000Z  Arooj Aftab
01a1f16f-9c7d-733a-ba51-db13974977de  tickets.ticket  2027-01-15T20:00:00.000Z  Nils Frahm   [archived]
01a1f16f-9c7c-74ba-ac82-919ada1113f9  tickets.ticket  2026-12-04T19:30:00.000Z  Khruangbin
```

</Terminal>

The kit compares each entry with the item it matches and writes only what differs, so a ticket the service didn't change is left alone and announces nothing. The kit also clears the earlier warning once a run finds no new edit.

</Step>
<Step>

### Read a failed run

Run the connector with a token the service refuses:

<Terminal>

```bash
MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600 MARFA_API_KEY=<connector key> \
  TICKETS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4100 TICKETS_TOKEN=wrong-token-1234 \
  node connectors/tickets/dist/main.js --once
```

```text
… error run failed: the ticket service answered 401; created 0, updated 0, archived 0, unchanged 0, skipped 0
```

</Terminal>

The process exits with status 1. The kit reported the run to your instance, so you can read it from any computer:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa connectors list
```

```text
id                                    source   name     last run  finished                  note
01a1f16f-9c3d-7407-91a3-a55d024651ea  tickets  tickets  failed    2026-11-19T01:33:50.787Z  the ticket service answered 401
```

</Terminal>

`marfa connectors runs` with the connector's ID lists its runs, newest first. The next run reads the service whole again, so a failure loses nothing.

When you're done, stop the ticket service with Control-C.

</Step>
